title: Self-driving cars and the last five per cent

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: The trial fleet's been running downtown for eight months now with no driver at all. Not even someone in the passenger seat.

turns.speaker: Max
turns.text: Downtown is the easy part, though. Slow, mapped to the centimetre, no snow.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: That's the whole story of this technology. Ninety-five per cent of driving was solved years ago and the last five per cent has taken a decade.

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: The safety numbers are good, to be fair. Fewer collisions per mile than human drivers in the same area.

turns.speaker: Max
turns.text: Fewer, but different. They fail in ways a person wouldn't, and that's what people can't stomach.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: Stopping dead in an intersection because a plastic bag blew past.

turns.speaker: Max
turns.text: Exactly. A human makes a bad judgement. The machine makes no judgement, which reads as worse even when it hurts fewer people.

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: I think that's the real obstacle and it isn't technical at all.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: There's a liability question underneath it too. When it does go wrong, who is actually in the dock?

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: The manufacturer, in the frameworks being drafted. Which they've accepted, surprisingly.

turns.speaker: Max
turns.text: They've accepted it because they think the numbers will be on their side.

turns.speaker: Theo
turns.text: And they might be. The thing nobody mentions is what happens to two million people who drive for a living.

turns.speaker: Rina
turns.text: No, that gets left for later, which is how it always goes.

points: A driverless fleet has run downtown for eight months, in conditions Max calls the easy case: slow, precisely mapped and snow-free.
Theo characterises the technology as having solved ninety-five per cent of driving quickly and spent a decade on the rest.
Safety data shows fewer collisions per mile than human drivers in the same area.
Max argues the obstacle is that machines fail differently, making no judgement rather than a poor one, which people find harder to accept.
Liability frameworks place responsibility on manufacturers, which they have accepted, in Max's view because they expect the statistics to favour them.
Theo raises the unaddressed employment consequences for people who drive for a living.
